sourceBoundary.included: Opening statements and first rebuttals only.
sourceBoundary.excluded: All subsequent audience questions, later replies, concessions, and closing comments; neither side is credited or penalized for excluded material.

files.anchor: Frozen reading-stage packet limits evidence to the approved formal-rounds source and withholds pass identities, totals, winners, and publication prose.
Manifest records lossless coverage of events 64–683, 17 moves, 11 audio checks, and seven unique audio responses.
Workflow requires two blinded judgments followed by anonymous dispute-only adjudication, with totals derived later in repository code.
Rubric evaluates six weighted dimensions move by move and separates logical coherence from evidential warrant.
Metadata identifies Atkins as pro and Law as con, with procedural handovers at events 199–200, 520–526, and 590.
Inventory metadata defines three burden bridges per side, six weighted sections, and complete approved-window coverage intervals.
Audio metadata reports all 11 triggered attribution and lexical checks resolved with no inventory change.
Events 64–208 contain Atkins's opening contrast between unconstrained speculation and evidence, scientific integration, domain loss, and optimism.
Events 209–347 contain Law's empirical-method concession, regress argument about ultimate explanation, and qualified is–ought argument.
Events 348–486 contain Law's mirror, kinship, river-identity, and mind–brain conceptual examples.
Events 487–626 finish Law's specialist-skill case, then contain Atkins's rebuttal and the beginning of Law's Galileo response.
Events 627–683 complete the linked-balls contradiction and distinguish causal origins of moral belief from normative justification.
Five pro opening moves cover evidential constraint, Aristotle, integrated science, shrinking philosophical domains, and scientific optimism.
Three con moves concede science's empirical strength while presenting ultimate-explanation and is–ought limits.
Four con moves develop mirror and identity analysis, a mind–body conceptual obstacle, and specialist philosophical skill.
Four rebuttal moves address fundamental origins, empirical study of morality, dismissal of conceptualism, and Galileo's thought experiment.
Final move argues that explaining moral-belief origins does not justify the moral positions themselves.
Five confirmed checks clarify the uncertain adjective in Atkins's opening, the integrated-domain wording, Law's empirical concession, and 'brute fact.'
Six confirmed checks restore dropped negatives, 'interim,' Uri Geller, River Thames, Galileo/Aristotle/Pisa, and Hume.
Audio segments begin Atkins's evidence passage and continue through the observation network and early domain-loss material.
Audio segments complete Atkins's domain-loss passage and carry Law from empirical scope through fundamental explanation and into morality.
Audio segments preserve Law's voting hypothetical with its negatives, then the river identity example and specialist-skill opening.
Audio segments finish Law's specialist-skill case, verify Atkins's River Thames dismissal, and preserve most of the Galileo and morality rebuttal.
Final audio segment states that causal moral origins do not make positions right or wrong and that justification requires a different argument.

neutralReadingStatement: All listed evidence-reading files were displayed completely in separate invocations. No anonymous dispute options, decision packet, canonical adjudication packet, primary judgments, scores, publication material, other debates, or excluded recording material was opened.
